items.title: Albert Warner Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: So I started playing with the college fellow, what you was calling there? Louis Demene and Eddie Jackson. So they sent downtown and got me. They were living uptown, so they said they wanted me to play with them. So I went on and started playing in a little band they had up there.

ctx.x: With Pete there, so we'd go to the barbershop on Bienville Street there. We'd rehearse a lot in there, him and I, just the bass and the trombone. So this fellow, Amos White. That's right. Amos White would come along, and he'd join in with us. And he would write off a little piece of music there and make me go over that music, you know. And so finally, I got pretty good with it. So this little band formed up. I went with them. They called it the Bulls Band. So I went on and started playing with them. So the first…
No name to it, just the?
